definition_zh: 先前的；更早的；优先的；更重要的；修道院院长；前科
definition_en: earlier in time or order, or higher in importance; also a monastic superior or a previous conviction
core_image: 排队时站在你前面的人，既更早到，也先被叫到
scene: 签约前，律师翻出旧协议。 The lawyer opened the prior agreement before signing, to be sure the new clauses did not contradict the old ones.
sceneCN: 这里 prior 是「先前的、更早的」（第 1 个义项：在时间上更早）；句意：律师在签字前翻出先前的协议，确认新条款不会与旧约定冲突。图中可辨识物件：旧合同、新合同、日期页、文件夹、律师的眼镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 先前的；更早的；优先的；更重要的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Earlier in time
senses.definition: existing or happening before something else
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物更早存在或发生
senses.example: She had prior experience in publishing.
senses.exampleCN: 她先前有出版经验。
senses.why: Latin prior is a comparative meaning 'former, first of two'. It compares two points on a line and names the one already passed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prior 是比较级，意为“前者、两者中的第一个”。它比较线上的两点，命名已经过去的那一点。

senses.title: Preceding in order
senses.definition: coming before in a series or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 在系列或程序中出现得更早
senses.example: No changes may be made without prior approval.
senses.exampleCN: 未经事先批准不得改动。
senses.why: Procedures require gates: the prior step must be completed before the next begins. The word turns sequence into a condition.
senses.whyCN: 程序需要关口：前一步必须完成，下一步才能开始。这个词把次序变成条件。

senses.title: Higher in importance or rank
senses.definition: having a stronger claim or higher rank
senses.definitionCN: 拥有更强的请求权或更高的等级
senses.example: They have a prior claim on the land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这块土地有更优先的请求权。
senses.why: The Latin comparative could mean 'superior' as well as 'earlier'. Priority and precedence share the image of standing in front of the line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁比较级既可指“更早”，也可指“更优越”。优先与居先共享“站在队伍前面”的意象。

senses.title: Before, in the phrase prior to
senses.definition: in formal usage, before a time or event
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法：在某个时间或事件之前
senses.example: Prior to 2010, the firm had no overseas office.
senses.exampleCN: 2010 年之前，这家公司没有海外办事处。
senses.why: Prior to is the formal cousin of before. Legal and academic writing prefer it because it sounds procedural rather than conversational.
senses.whyCN: prior to 是 before 的正式表亲。法律与学术写作偏爱它，因为它听起来像程序而非口语。

senses.title: Presumed or existing earlier
senses.definition: in formal contexts, already held or existing before the present matter
senses.definitionCN: 正式语境中，在当前事项之前已持有或已存在
senses.example: The prior agreement still governs the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 先前的协议仍管辖这场争议。
senses.why: Law speaks of prior agreements, prior art, and prior rights: things that existed first and therefore constrain what can be done now.
senses.whyCN: 法律谈 prior agreements、prior art、prior rights：先已存在的事物，因此约束当下能做什么。

senses.title: A monastic superior
senses.definition: the head of a priory or a religious house
senses.definitionCN: 小修道院或宗教院舍的首脑
senses.example: The prior welcomed the visitors at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 院长在门口迎接访客。
senses.why: The noun came into English in the 14c. from Medieval Latin prior, 'superior'. The monastic prior stands first in his house, the same rank image as the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词 14 世纪从中世纪拉丁语 prior“上级”进入英语。修道院院长在其院舍中居首，与形容词的等级意象相同。

senses.title: A previous conviction (informal)
senses.definition: in informal legal usage, an earlier criminal conviction
senses.definitionCN: 非正式法律用语：先前的刑事定罪
senses.example: The defendant has two priors.
senses.exampleCN: 被告有两项前科。
senses.why: Police and court slang clip the phrase 'prior conviction' to priors. The word's temporal sense becomes a record that follows a person.
senses.whyCN: 警察与法庭俚语把 prior conviction 缩略为 priors。这个词的时间义变成一份跟随此人的记录。

senses.title: The antecedent in logic
senses.definition: in logic, the proposition from which another is inferred
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中推出另一命题所依据的前一命题
senses.example: If the prior is false, the conclusion fails.
senses.exampleCN: 如果前件为假，结论就不成立。
senses.why: Inference runs along a line: the prior proposition comes first and licenses the next. The temporal order becomes a relation of support.
senses.whyCN: 推理沿一条线运行：前件在先，并授权后件。时间次序变成支撑关系。

senses.title: Superior in rank (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, of higher rank or dignity
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：等级或尊严更高的
senses.example: the prior rank of a duke
senses.exampleCN: 公爵更高的等级
senses.why: This is the Latin comparative at full strength: prior as 'superior'. Modern English keeps the trace in the noun prior and in the idea of a prior claim.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁比较级的完整力量：prior 即“更优越”。现代英语在名词 prior 与“更优先的请求权”中留下痕迹。

intro.en: Prior entered English twice: first as a noun for a monastic superior, then as an adjective for 'earlier'. Both come from Latin prior, a comparative meaning 'former, first of two', which also gives priority and primacy.
intro.cn: prior 两次进入英语：先作名词指修道院院长，后作形容词指“更早”。两者都来自拉丁语 prior——一个意为“前者、两者中第一”的比较级，它也生成 priority 与 primacy。

items.en: The noun is first recorded for the superior of a priory or religious house, from Medieval Latin prior.
items.cn: 名词最早记录指小修道院或宗教院舍的上级，来自中世纪拉丁语 prior。

items.en: Latin prior 'former, previous, first of two' is a comparative of an old adjective *pri- 'before'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 prior“前者、先前的、两者中第一”是古形容词 *pri-“在前”的比较级。

items.en: The root is traced to PIE *per- 'before, first', also behind first, prime, and principal. The reconstruction is standard.
items.cn: 词根被追溯到原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”，也见于 first、prime、principal。该重构是通行说法。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English with the sense 'earlier, previous'.
items.cn: 形容词在英语中记录为“更早的、先前的”。

items.en: prior to becomes a formal preposition, and the legal phrase prior claim spreads.
items.cn: prior to 成为正式介词，法律短语 prior claim 传播开来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the religious noun and the temporal adjective side by side, plus the informal plural priors for convictions.
items.cn: 现代英语让宗教名词与时间形容词并存，另有口语复数 priors 指前科。

note.en: The first group shares the prior/priority stem; the second is about words that also mean earlier or more important.
note.cn: 第一组共享 prior/priority 词干，第二组看同样表示“更早”或“更重要”的词。

entries.definition: the state of being first in rank or the thing ranked first. It comes from Medieval Latin prioritas.
entries.definitionCN: 优先地位；优先事项。来自中世纪拉丁语 prioritas。

entries.definition: a small monastery headed by a prior.
entries.definitionCN: 由院长主持的小修道院。

entries.definition: a female superior of a priory.
earlier, especially the one just before. It is less formal than prior.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的，尤指刚过去的那一个。它比 prior 少些正式。

entries.definition: the earlier of two, or a past role-holder. It contrasts with latter.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中在前的，或前任。与 latter 相对。

entries.definition: coming immediately before in order. It is purely positional.
entries.definitionCN: 在次序上紧接其前。它纯粹是位置性的。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin prior as a comparative, the noun for a monastic superior, the phrase prior to, and the legal sense of a prior claim.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 prior 的比较级性质、指修道院院长的名词、短语 prior to，以及 prior claim 的法律义。

normal.en: Prior is a Latin comparative: it compares two things and names the earlier one.
normal.cn: prior 是拉丁比较级：它比较两物，并命名更早的那一个。

normal.en: The same comparative can mean 'superior', which is why prior also means 'more important'.
normal.cn: 同一比较级也可指“更优越”，所以 prior 也表“更重要”。

normal.en: The noun prior is a different borrowing: the head of a priory stands first in his house.
normal.cn: 名词 prior 是另一次借入：小修道院院长在其院舍中居首。

normal.en: Prior to is formal 'before'; lawyers and academics prefer it to sound procedural.
normal.cn: prior to 是正式的 before；律师与学者偏爱它，以显得程序化。

normal.en: In police slang, priors are prior convictions: the past that follows a person.
normal.cn: 警察俚语中，priors 是前科：跟随一个人的过去。

abstract.en: Time and rank collapse into one word: what came first is assumed to deserve first place.
abstract.cn: 时间与等级在此塌缩成一个词：先来的，被假定该先得。

abstract.en: A prior claim is a promise the past makes to the present.
abstract.cn: 优先请求权是过去对当下作出的承诺。

abstract.en: The comparative form is the point: prior never stands alone, it always implies a second term.
abstract.cn: 重点在比较级形式：prior 从不孤立，它总隐含另一个项。

examples.en: You need prior approval before changing the budget.
examples.cn: 改动预算前需要事先批准。

examples.en: Prior to joining the firm, she taught at a university.
examples.cn: 加入这家公司之前，她在大学任教。

examples.en: The court considered his prior convictions.
examples.cn: 法庭考虑了他的前科。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来尔”——先扑过来排队的那一个 → prior 先前的、优先的

root: 拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”，是 *pri-“在前”的比较级；更早为原始印欧语 *per-。同族有 priority、prime、principal。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of prior, all comparative. The word always implies a second term: this one is earlier, or higher, or both. It can point to a time, a rank, a right, a monastic office, or a criminal record.
sensesIntro.cn: prior 的九个义项都是比较性的。这个词总隐含另一个项：这一个更早，或更高，或两者兼有。它可以指时间、等级、权利、修道职务或犯罪记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one standing earlier in the line, and therefore first in line.
core.cn: 核心意象：在队伍中站得更早、因而更靠前的那一个。

branches.en: TIME: an earlier point or step, including agreements already in force.
branches.cn: 时间：更早的时间点或步骤，包括已生效的协议。

branches.en: RANK: the comparative shades into superiority and precedence.
branches.cn: 等级：比较级滑向优越与居先。

branches.en: PREPOSITION: prior to is the formal 'before'.
branches.cn: 介词：prior to 是正式的“在……之前”。

branches.en: OFFICE: the monastic prior stands first in his house.

senses.title: Ordinary people
senses.definition: ordinary people, especially of a region

senses.why: This is the oldest general sense.

senses.title: Traditional
senses.definition: belonging to the traditional culture of ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 属于普通人传统文化的
senses.example: These songs are traditional folk music.

senses.why: The people's culture is called folk culture.
senses.whyCN: 人民的文化被称为民间文化。

senses.title: Folk music
senses.definition: music in the traditional style of a community
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体传统风格的音乐
senses.example: She plays folk at the café.
senses.exampleCN: 她在咖啡馆演奏民谣。
senses.why: The adjective shortens into a noun for the genre.
senses.whyCN: 形容词缩短为该流派的名称。

senses.title: Family
senses.definition: one's family or relatives, in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中指家人或亲戚
senses.example: I am visiting my folks this weekend.

senses.why: The plural folks often means family.

intro.cn: folk 来自古英语中表示民族或人群的词。

items.en: Folc meant people or a nation.

items.en: Fulkam carried the same group sense.

items.en: Folk named common people and their customs.
items.cn: folk 指普通民众及其习俗。

items.en: Folk music and folklore named traditions.
items.cn: folk music 与 folklore 命名传统。

items.en: Folks became an informal word for family.

note.en: Folk is compared with similar-looking words and with words for people and tradition.
note.cn: 把 folk 与形近词以及表示人和传统的词作比较。

human beings in general

normalIntro.en: Folk is the people and everything they pass down by voice.
normalIntro.cn: folk 是人民，以及他们口口相传的一切。

normal.en: Folk songs tell old stories.
normal.cn: 民谣讲述古老故事。

normal.en: Local folk know the river well.
normal.cn: 当地人对这条河很熟悉。

normal.en: She studies folk art.

normal.en: Old folk need a place to sit.
normal.cn: 老人需要坐的地方。

normal.en: My folks live in the country.
normal.cn: 我家人住在乡下。

abstract.en: Folk memory keeps what history forgets.
abstract.cn: 民间记忆保存了历史遗忘的东西。

abstract.en: A song belongs to everyone who sings it.
abstract.cn: 一首歌属于每个唱它的人。

abstract.en: Folk culture has no single author.
abstract.cn: 民间文化没有唯一的作者。

root: 源自古英语 folc（人民、民族），核心义「普通人群及其传统」。

sensesIntro.cn: folk 意为人们、民间的、民谣或家人。

core.en: Ordinary people and what they hand down.

branches.en: Culture passed down by ordinary people.

branches.en: Family in everyday speech.

definition_en: at the beginning of a process or period, before later changes
core_image: 一条跑道的起点白线，前方是尚未跑过的路
scene: 项目启动会上，负责人先回顾最早的安排。 Initially, the factory produced only hand tools.
sceneCN: 这里指过程刚开始时的情况（第 2 个义项：句首交代最初阶段）；句意为这家工厂起初只生产手工工具。

senses.title: At the first stage
senses.definition: at the beginning of a process, before later changes
senses.definitionCN: 在过程开始时，后来尚未发生改动之前
senses.example: The building was initially designed as a warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑最初是按仓库设计的。
senses.why: Modifying the verb, it fixes the starting state and leaves room for a later revision.
senses.whyCN: 修饰动词时，它固定了起始状态，并为后来的改动留下余地。

senses.title: Sentence-opening frame
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to set the opening scene of an account
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，为一段叙述搭起开场的场景
senses.example: Initially, no one believed the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 起初，没有人相信那个传闻。
senses.why: The sentence adverb organizes the order of events for the reader rather than describing how an action was done.
senses.whyCN: 这个句子副词为读者安排事件顺序，而不是描述动作怎么做。

senses.title: First but not now
senses.definition: used to contrast an early state with a later reversal
senses.definitionCN: 用来把早期状态与后来的反转形成对照
senses.example: She initially opposed the merger, then voted for it.
senses.exampleCN: 她起初反对合并，后来却投了赞成票。
senses.why: The word carries an implicature of change: naming the first position invites the reader to expect a second.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带有「后来变了」的言外之意：说出最初的立场，读者自然会期待后文。

senses.title: At the outset of a period
senses.definition: at the very start of a defined period such as a career or project
senses.definitionCN: 在某段明确时期的最开端，如职业生涯或项目
senses.example: The firm initially employed only five people.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司最初只雇了五个人。
senses.why: Here the word anchors a timeline, often with numbers or dates, and does not by itself suggest a reversal.
senses.whyCN: 这里它锚定一条时间线，常与数字或日期连用，本身并不暗示后来的反转。

senses.title: First step in a procedure
senses.definition: used in instructions to mark the first operation in a sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在说明中标记一系列操作的第一步
senses.example: Initially, the sample is heated to a fixed temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 首先，把样品加热到固定温度。
senses.why: Technical writing uses it as a sequence marker, close to first, with the other steps assumed to follow.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作把它当作顺序标记，接近「首先」，并默认后续步骤会接着进行。

senses.title: Originally intended
senses.definition: used with verbs of planning to describe an intention later abandoned
senses.definitionCN: 与计划类动词连用，描述后来被放弃的意图
senses.example: The site was initially intended for a small clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地原本打算建一间小诊所。
senses.why: With plan, intend or design, the word signals unrealized intention rather than a completed early stage.
senses.whyCN: 与「计划、打算、设计」连用时，它暗示意图没有实现，而不是描述已完成的早期阶段。

senses.title: On first impression
senses.definition: used of an impression formed before closer inspection
senses.definitionCN: 用于尚未细看时形成的印象
senses.example: The poem initially looks like a simple folk song.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗初看像一首简单的民歌。
senses.why: The adverb can mark a first reading or impression that later analysis may overturn.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以标记初次阅读或第一印象，而后续分析可能把它推翻。

senses.title: Initial conditions in science
senses.definition: in technical contexts, describing the state of a system at the starting point of an analysis
senses.definitionCN: 在技术语境中，描述系统在分析起点时的状态
senses.example: The model is initially at rest and then subjected to a steady force.
senses.exampleCN: 模型初始时静止，随后受到一个恒定的力。
senses.why: Physics and mathematics use the word for the state assigned at the start of an analysis, a precise technical sense rather than a narrative one.
senses.whyCN: 物理与数学用它指分析起点所设定的状态，这是精确的技术义，而非叙述义。

intro.en: Initially is the Latin adjective for a beginning plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词是拉丁语「属于开端的」形容词加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The noun initium means a beginning or entrance, and supplies the stem for the whole family.
items.cn: 名词意为「开端、进入」，为整个词族提供词干。

items.en: The verb inire joins in-, meaning into, with ire, to go; literally to go into something.
items.cn: 动词由表示「进入」的前缀与「走」合成，字面是「走进某事物」。

items.en: The adjective initialis, belonging to a beginning, is formed on the noun stem.
items.cn: 形容词由名词词干构成，意为「属于开端的」。

items.en: French initial and English initial carry the adjective into general and technical use.
items.cn: 法语与英语的形容词把它带入通用与技术语境。

items.en: English adds its adverb suffix and uses the form to frame the first stage of an account; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语加副词后缀，用它框定叙述的最初阶段；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern scientific writing fixes initially for the state assigned at the start of an experiment or model.
items.cn: 现代科学写作把它固定为实验或模型开始时所设定的状态。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin beginning-stem; the second group names ways of pointing to the first point in time.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「开端」词干；第二组是指向时间上最初时点的近义说法。

entries.definition: Happening at the beginning; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 发生在开端的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The act of starting something or the ceremony of admission.
entries.definitionCN: 开始某事的行为，或加入仪式的入门礼。

entries.definition: The ability to act first, or a new plan set in motion.
entries.definitionCN: 率先行动的能力，或启动的新计划。

entries.definition: To prepare a system or variable for its first use.
entries.definitionCN: 为系统或变量首次使用作准备；初始化。

entries.definition: At the beginning, especially before a change becomes clear.
entries.definitionCN: 开始时，尤指在变化显现之前。

entries.definition: In the first place, before later alteration.
At the very beginning of an undertaking.
entries.definitionCN: 在一项工作最开始的时候。

entries.definition: Before anything else in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 在时间或次序上先于其他。

entries.definition: During the first part of a period or process.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时期或过程的前段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real going-in root and the real patterns of planning and science.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「走进」词根，以及计划与科学语境中的真实搭配。

normal.en: The root means to go in, so initially names the moment just inside the door.
normal.cn: 词根意为「走进」，所以「最初」就是刚迈进门口的那一刻。

normal.en: Put it first in a sentence and the story is quietly rewound.
normal.cn: 把它放在句首，故事就被悄悄倒带。

normal.en: Say how things were initially and the reader waits for a later turn.
normal.cn: 先说最初怎样，读者自然会等「后来怎样」。

normal.en: In a laboratory report it is the moment the clock starts.
normal.cn: 在实验报告里，它就是计时器归零的那一瞬。

normal.en: With intend or plan it hints that the intention was later dropped.
normal.cn: 与「打算、计划」连用时，它暗示这个意图后来没照做。

abstract.en: The first stage is not yet the story; it is the position from which the story will be measured.
abstract.cn: 最初阶段还不是故事本身，而是后来用来丈量故事的那个起点。

abstract.en: Naming how something began is already admitting that it did not stay that way.
abstract.cn: 说出某事的开始，本身就已经承认它没有一直如此。

abstract.en: An initial state is a clean sheet that later events will mark.
abstract.cn: 初始状态是一张白纸，等着后来的事件在上面落笔。

examples.en: The committee initially approved the plan, then reversed itself in June.
examples.cn: 委员会起初批准了这项计划，六月又推翻了它。

examples.en: The device is initially calibrated at room temperature.
examples.cn: 这台设备最初在室温下校准。

examples.en: Initially, the course was offered only to graduate students.
examples.cn: 起初，这门课只向研究生开放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一你手里」——一开始手里什么都没有，只是起点

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses cover the first stage, the sentence-opening frame, the implication of later change, the start of a period, the first step of a procedure, an abandoned intention, first impression and initial conditions in science.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项覆盖最初阶段、句首框架、后来改变的含义、某段时期的开端、程序第一步、被放弃的意图、初看印象，以及科学中的初始条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white starting line on a track, with the road still unrun ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑道起点的一条白线，前方是尚未跑过的路。

branches.en: THE FIRST STAGE: the starting state of a process before revision.
branches.cn: 最初阶段：过程开始、尚未改动时的状态。

branches.en: THE NARRATIVE FRAME: the sentence-opening marker and the hint of a later reversal.
branches.cn: 叙述框架：句首标记与「后来反转」的暗示。

branches.en: THE PERIOD OUTSET: the first point on a timeline.
branches.cn: 时期开端：时间线上的第一个点。

branches.en: THE PLANNED BEGINNING: the first procedural step and the intention later dropped.
branches.cn: 计划中的开始：程序第一步，以及后来放弃的意图。

branches.en: THE FIRST READING: first impression and the assigned initial state of a system.
branches.cn: 初次判读：初看印象，以及系统被设定的初始状态。

intro.en: Initially is built from the Latin beginning-stem, its adjective suffix and an English adverb suffix; the parts recur across the family.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「开端」词干、形容词后缀与英语副词后缀构成，各构件在同一词族中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: The family starts from the verb for going in and builds a noun of beginning, then an adjective of belonging to the beginning.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从表示「走进」的动词出发，先构成「开端」名词，再构成「属于开端」的形容词。

items.example: The prefix gives the direction of entering.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出「进入」的方向。

items.example: The verb supplies the movement at the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供整个词族的核心动作。

items.example: The noun turns the movement into a starting point.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把动作转成一个起点。

items.example: The adjective attaches the idea to whatever comes first.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把这一概念系到最先出现的事物上。

items.example: The verb gives the family its noun of initiation.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为词族提供「入门、开始」的名词。

items.example: English keeps the adjective for what comes first.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留这个形容词指最先出现的事物。

items.example: The verb is used for starting a process or admitting a member.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用于发起过程或接纳成员。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a time adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成时间副词。

items.meaning: the act of setting a starting state
items.example: Computing uses the noun for setting a system to its start.
items.exampleCN: 计算机领域用这个名词指把系统设回起始状态。

definition_en: a strong effect on someone or something, or the force of one object hitting another
core_image: 石子落进水塘，圈纹一圈圈推到岸边
scene: 新地铁线开通三个月后，站边小店换了两轮老板。 The impact on the neighbourhood was clear from the empty shops and the new coffee queue.
sceneCN: 这里 impact 是「影响」（第 1 个义项：对人或事产生的强烈作用），句意是对这一带的影响从空掉的店铺和新排起的咖啡队就能看出。画面里有地铁口的波纹状人潮。

senses.title: A strong effect
senses.definition: a powerful effect that something has on a situation or person
senses.definitionCN: 某物对局势或人产生的强烈作用
senses.example: The new policy had an impact on small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策对小店产生了影响。
senses.why: The word began as physical striking and was carried over to anything that strikes a situation the way a stone strikes water.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指实物的撞击，后来扩展到一切像石子击水般击中局面的东西。

senses.title: The force of a collision
senses.definition: the moment and force of one body striking another
senses.definitionCN: 一个物体击中另一物体的即刻与力度
senses.example: The windscreen cracked on impact.
senses.exampleCN: 挡风玻璃一撞就裂了。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, kept in physics and in accident reports.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，保留在物理学与事故报道里。

senses.title: To affect or to hit
senses.definition: to have an effect on something, or to strike it forcefully
senses.definitionCN: 对某物产生影响，或用力撞上
senses.example: Rising costs impact every household.
senses.exampleCN: 成本上涨冲击着每一个家庭。
senses.why: English turns almost any strong noun into a verb, and impact took that route in the twentieth century.
senses.whyCN: 英语几乎能把任何强势名词变动词，impact 在二十世纪就走上了这条路。

intro.en: Impact began as a Latin participle meaning driven in or pressed against, and only later became a noun for effect.
intro.cn: impact 最初是拉丁语分词，意为「打入、压向」，后来才成为表示「影响」的名词。

items.en: Pangere meant to fasten or strike, and its participle pactus described something fixed or driven in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pangere 意为固定或击打，其分词 pactus 描述被钉入或压紧之物。

items.en: Impactus was the strengthened form, pressed hard against something.
items.cn: impactus 是加强形式，意为被重重压向某物。

items.en: English took impact in the seventeenth century as a term in mechanics for collision.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪以力学用语的「碰撞」义引入 impact。

items.en: In the twentieth century it broadened into the general sense of a strong effect.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，它扩展为泛指强烈影响。

items.en: Verb use grew after the 1950s and is now common in business writing.
items.cn: 动词用法在1950年代后增多，如今在商务写作中很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same pacting root; the near-meaning group gathers words for effect.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「钉入、击打」词根的词；近义组收表示作用的词。

entries.definition: An agreement fixed between parties, from the same root.
Pressed closely together, sharing the fastening root.
entries.definitionCN: 紧压在一起的，同出「紧固」之根。

entries.definition: The state of being wedged or pressed in, especially in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 被卡住压紧的状态，多用于医学。

entries.definition: A result caused by something; quieter than impact.
entries.definitionCN: 由某物引起的结果，语气比 impact 平。

entries.definition: The power to change how someone acts or thinks.
entries.definitionCN: 改变他人行为或想法的力量。

entries.definition: The physical crashing of two objects, close to sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 两个物体的实体相撞，接近第二个义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks join the Latin fastening root to ripples on a pond and to business verb use.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把拉丁「钉紧」词根连到水塘涟漪与商务动词用法上。

normal.en: The root pact means fixed together, as in a peace pact; impact is a blow that fixes a mark.
normal.cn: 词根 pact 意为固定在一起，如和平协定；impact 是留下痕迹的击打。

normal.en: Noun stress first: IM-pact; verb often the same in modern English.
normal.cn: 名词重音在前：IM-pact；现代英语动词常同音。

normal.en: Have an impact on is the safest phrase: preposition on, not for.
normal.cn: 最稳的搭配是 have an impact on，介词用 on。

normal.en: On impact is the expression in crash reports.
normal.cn: 事故报道里用 on impact 表示「撞击时」。

normal.en: A stone, a policy and a rumour can all make the same ripples.
normal.cn: 石子、政策与谣言都能激起同样的涟漪。

abstract.en: The word began with bodies meeting and ended with lives meeting, and the physics stayed.
abstract.cn: 这个词起于物体相遇，终于人生相遇，而那点物理学一直留着。

abstract.en: Impact measures what something leaves behind, so every use implies a before and an after.
abstract.cn: impact 衡量某物留下了什么，因此每次使用都隐含一个之前与一个之后。

abstract.en: A policy with no impact has failed quietly, and a person with impact has changed the room on entering.
abstract.cn: 毫无影响的政策是悄悄失败了，而有影响力的人一进屋就改变了房间。

examples.en: The report examines the impact of tourism on the coast.
examples.cn: 这份报告考察旅游业对海岸的影响。

examples.en: The car hit the barrier and the driver was thrown forward on impact.
examples.cn: 汽车撞上护栏，撞击时司机被向前抛出。

examples.en: Rising fuel prices impacted the whole industry.
examples.cn: 燃料涨价冲击了整个行业。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + pact 压紧（如 pact 协定）——狠狠压进去，即撞击；引申为冲击、影响

root: 拉丁语 pangere「钉入、击打」→ 分词 impactus「被压向的」，十七世纪进入英语作力学用语，二十世纪扩展为「影响」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a strong effect, a physical collision, and the verb made from both.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：强烈影响、实体撞击，以及由两者转来的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ripples from a dropped stone reaching the bank.
core.cn: 核心意象：石子落水后，涟漪一直推到岸边。

branches.en: THE POLICY LINE: the word asks what changed after the decision.
branches.cn: 政策线：这个词问的是决定之后改变了什么。

branches.en: THE ACCIDENT LINE: on impact reports the instant of collision.
branches.cn: 事故线：on impact 报告相撞的一瞬。

branches.en: THE BUSINESS LINE: impact as a verb suits reports and meetings.
branches.cn: 商务线：impact 作动词适合理报告与开会。

branches.en: THE FORCE LINE: both senses carry a sense of something arriving hard.
branches.cn: 力量线：两种用法都带着「重重抵达」之感。

branches.en: THE RIPPLE LINE: the noun and verb name cause and consequence.
branches.cn: 涟漪线：名词与动词分别命名起因与后果。

intro.en: Impact is a Latin participle used as a noun, with a small modern family including a back-formed verb.
intro.cn: impact 是当作名词用的拉丁分词，现代又反向造出动词，形成一个小家族。

latinIntro.en: Pangere and impactus are recorded in Latin, and pact- supplies the fixed-agreement branch of the family.
latinIntro.cn: pangere 与 impactus 均有拉丁文献，pact- 这一支则长出「订约」的意义。

items.example: Import carries a similar inward sense.
items.exampleCN: import 也有类似的向内感。

items.example: The impact was felt for years.
The area was badly impacted by the flood.
items.exampleCN: 这一带受洪水影响严重。
他们想要一个有力的开场。

items.example: The two sides signed a pact.

definition_zh: 接待；招待会；前台；接收；反响
definition_en: the act of welcoming someone; a formal party; the desk where visitors arrive; the catching of signals; the response of an audience
core_image: 酒店大堂前台亮着灯的柜台
scene: 酒店大堂里，客人排在前台登记，行李箱靠在一旁。 Guests waited at the reception desk for their room keys.
sceneCN: 这里 reception 修饰 desk，指「前台」（第 3 个义项：接待处）；句意为客人们在前台等候领取房卡。画面里可留意：亮着灯的前台柜台、靠在一旁的行李箱。

pos.zh: 接待；招待会；前台；接收；反响

senses.title: The act of welcoming someone
senses.definition: the act of greeting and welcoming a person who arrives
senses.definitionCN: 迎接并款待到来之人的行为
senses.example: The mayor gave the visitors a warm reception.
senses.exampleCN: 市长热情接待了来访者。
senses.why: The Latin noun receptio named a taking in, and a welcome is the human form of that taking in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 receptio 指「收进来」，而迎接正是这种「收进来」的人际形式。

senses.title: A formal party
senses.definition: a formal social gathering held to welcome guests or mark an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 为迎接客人或纪念某事而举行的正式社交聚会
senses.example: They held a reception after the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式结束后他们举行了一场招待会。
senses.why: A party is a welcome made visible in a room, with food, light, and guests standing together.
senses.whyCN: 招待会是把「欢迎」显现在一个房间里：食物、灯光与站在一起的宾客。

senses.title: The front desk
senses.definition: the desk or area where visitors are received in a hotel or office
senses.definitionCN: 酒店或办公楼里接待来访者的柜台或区域
senses.example: Guests waited at the reception desk for their room keys.
senses.exampleCN: 客人们在前台等候领取房卡。
senses.why: The place where receiving happens took the name of the act, so the desk itself became the reception.
senses.whyCN: 负责接待的地方借用了行为之名，于是柜台本身也被称为 reception。

senses.title: The catching of signals
senses.definition: the quality or act of receiving broadcast or electronic signals
senses.definitionCN: 接收广播或电子信号的行为或质量
senses.example: Poor reception made the call hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 信号不好，那通电话很难听清。
senses.why: A radio takes a signal in just as a host takes a guest in, so the technical sense grew from the same image.
senses.whyCN: 收音机收进信号，正如主人迎进客人，技术义正从同一形象生长出来。

senses.title: The response of an audience
senses.definition: the way people react to a performance, a book, or an idea
senses.definitionCN: 人们对于演出、书籍或观念的反应方式
senses.example: The novel received a mixed reception.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说得到的反响褒贬不一。
senses.why: To receive a work is to let it in and judge it, so reception came to mean the judgment of an audience.
senses.whyCN: 接受一部作品，就是让它进来并加以评判，于是 reception 引申为观众的评价。

intro.en: Reception is the noun of receiving: it names the act, the party, the desk, the signal, and the audience response.
intro.cn: reception 是「接收」的名词：它命名行为、宴会、柜台、信号，以及观众的反响。

items.en: Recipere meant to take in or receive, from re- and capere, to take.
items.cn: recipere 意为收进或接收，由 re- 与 capere（拿取）构成。

items.en: Receptio named the act of taking something or someone in.
items.cn: receptio 指把某物或某人收进来的行为。

items.en: Old French reception carried both the welcome and the technical sense.
items.cn: 古法语 reception 同时带有欢迎与技术两层含义。

items.en: Middle English reception named a welcome and a formal gathering.
items.cn: 中古英语 reception 指欢迎，也指正式聚会。

items.en: Modern English added the front desk, radio signals, and public response.
items.cn: 现代英语又加入了前台、无线电信号与公众反响。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for welcome, party, and response.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的名词；近义组收表欢迎、聚会与反响的词。

entries.definition: The way something is understood.
The forming of an idea.
The act of misleading.
A greeting given to a newcomer.
A social gathering.
A entrance hall or waiting area.
A reaction to something.

normalIntro.en: The word is receiving made into a noun, and the same act stretches from people to signals to reviews.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「接收」的名词化，同一个行为从人延伸到信号，再到评论。

normal.en: Receive plus -tion: the act of taking in.
normal.cn: receive 加 -tion：收进来这一行为。

normal.en: Reception desk is the first place a visitor meets in a hotel.
normal.cn: reception desk 是客人在酒店最先遇到的地方。

normal.en: A wedding reception is a party that welcomes guests after the vows.
normal.cn: wedding reception 是仪式后迎接宾客的宴会。

normal.en: Radio reception depends on the aerial, not on manners.
normal.cn: radio reception 取决于天线，而不取决于礼貌。

normal.en: A mixed reception means some liked the work and some did not.
normal.cn: a mixed reception 意为有人喜欢这部作品，有人不喜欢。

abstract.en: Every reception is a decision about what to let in.
abstract.cn: 每一次接待，都是关于让什么进来的决定。

abstract.en: A cold reception can freeze an idea before it grows.
abstract.cn: 冷淡的反响能在观念成长之前把它冻住。

abstract.en: The way a work is received is part of what the work becomes.
abstract.cn: 一部作品被接受的方式，构成了它最终的样子。

examples.en: The mayor gave the visitors a warm reception.
examples.cn: 市长热情接待了来访者。

examples.en: Guests waited at the reception desk for their room keys.
examples.cn: 客人们在前台等候领取房卡。

examples.en: The novel received a mixed reception.
examples.cn: 这部小说得到的反响褒贬不一。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 cept（拿取）加 ion（行为）：把客人接进来是接待，把信号接进来是接收，招待会也是把人迎来。

root: 拉丁 recipere（接收）→ 拉丁 receptio（接待）→ 古法语 reception → 英语 reception；同族有 receive、receiver、receptive。

sensesIntro.en: The core is taking someone or something in; the senses move from a welcome to a party, a desk, a signal, and a public response.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把某人或某物收进来」；义项从欢迎，到宴会、前台、信号，再到公众反响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit desk in a hotel lobby, keys laid out for arriving guests.
core.cn: 核心意象：酒店大堂里亮着灯的前台，房卡摆给到来的客人。

branches.en: a handshake at the door
branches.cn: 门口的一次握手

branches.en: candles and guests in a hall
branches.cn: 厅里烛光与宾客

branches.en: keys waiting on a counter
branches.cn: 柜台上待取的房卡

branches.en: an aerial on the roof
branches.cn: 屋顶上的天线

branches.en: a row of reviews in a paper
branches.cn: 报纸上排开的评论

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin verb of taking, and the noun ending turns the act into a place, an event, and a response.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语的「拿取」动词上，名词词尾把行为变成场所、事件与反响。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is recipere and its noun receptio; the ending -tion came through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 recipere 及其名词 receptio；词尾 -tion 经法语而来。

definition_zh: 承认；认错；准许进入；接纳；容纳；容许；采纳
definition_en: to agree that something is true, or to allow a person or thing to enter
core_image: 守门人侧身让路，把门外的人与门外的事实一并放进来
scene: 病房外的长椅上，家属等着护士叫名字。 She was admitted to hospital late that night with a high fever.
sceneCN: 这里 admitted 是被医院收下住院（第 4 个义项：被机构接纳，如入院、入学）；句意为她那天深夜因高烧住进了医院。

pos.zh: 动词：承认；准许进入；接纳；容纳
动词：承认（admit to）；容许（admit of）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁名词 admissio 而来，义为「承认；进入许可；入场费」
由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「进入权；进入」
由过去分词加 -ly 构成，义为「诚然；无可否认地」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的；可接受的」

senses.title: To agree that something is true
senses.definition: to agree, often unwillingly, that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 往往不情愿地同意某事为真
senses.example: He finally admitted that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他最终承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: Admittere is 'to let in': a fact you have kept outside the door is allowed through, and the verb names that inward movement rather than the fact itself.
senses.whyCN: admittere 是「放进来」：一个被你挡在门外的事实获准通过，这个动词命名的是「往里放」的动作，而不是事实本身。

senses.title: To confess to a fault
senses.definition: to say that you have done something wrong or illegal
senses.definitionCN: 说出自己做过错事或违法的事
senses.example: She admitted taking the money from the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认拿了抽屉里的钱。
senses.why: The door is the same, but what passes through is your own fault: you stop guarding it and let it into the record, which is why admit to is the usual pattern.
senses.whyCN: 门还是那扇门，只是通过的是自己的过错：你不再把它守住，而是让它进入记录，所以这个义项常用 admit to 这个结构。

senses.title: To allow someone to enter a place
senses.definition: to allow a person or thing to enter a building, room or other place
senses.definitionCN: 允许人或物进入某座建筑、某个房间或其他场所
senses.example: The usher admitted us through a side door.
senses.exampleCN: 引座员让我们从侧门进去了。
senses.why: This is the plain physical sense of mittere with ad-: a person is sent in, and the verb records the doorkeeper's decision to let them pass.
senses.whyCN: 这是 mittere 加 ad- 最朴素的物理义：一个人被送进门内，动词记下的就是守门人放行的决定。

senses.title: To accept someone into an institution
senses.definition: to accept someone into a hospital, school, club or other institution, very often in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 接纳某人进入医院、学校、社团等机构，常用被动形式
senses.example: Only twelve students are admitted to the programme each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目每年只录取十二名学生。
senses.why: An institution is a door with rules attached: to be admitted is to be let through those rules, whether the place waiting is a hospital bed or a seat in a class.
senses.whyCN: 机构是一扇挂着规矩的门：被接纳就是被放行通过这些规矩，门外等着的可能是一张病床，也可能是一个课桌位。

senses.title: To have room for a number of people
senses.definition: of a hall, room or vehicle, to have space for a certain number of people
senses.definitionCN: 指厅堂、房间或车辆能装下一定数量的人
senses.example: The hall admits up to five hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅最多可容纳五百人。
senses.why: The metaphor turns around here: the building becomes the doorkeeper, and the number it admits is simply the number its space can let through.
senses.whyCN: 比喻在这里转了个方向：建筑本身成了守门人，它能「放进来」的人数，就是它的空间能放过的人数。

senses.title: To allow something to be possible
senses.definition: to allow the possibility of something, used especially in the phrase admit of
senses.definitionCN: 容许某事存在可能性，尤用于 admit of 这一结构
senses.example: The evidence admits of only one explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 这些证据只容许一种解释。
senses.why: If a door can let something through, a situation can also let a reading through; the negative admits of no delay means the door is firmly shut.
senses.whyCN: 如果一扇门能放东西通过，一种情况也能放过某种解读；否定形式 admits of no delay 就是说这扇门关得死死的，一点余地都没有。

senses.title: To allow evidence in court
senses.definition: of a court or judge, to allow evidence or an argument to be considered officially
senses.definitionCN: 指法院或法官允许把某项证据、主张正式纳入审理
senses.example: The judge admitted the recording as evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 法官采纳了那段录音作为证据。
senses.why: Legal procedure borrows the doorway: evidence stands outside until the rules of admissibility let it in, and the ruling that opens the door is called an admission.
senses.whyCN: 法律程序借用了这道门：证据本来站在门外，直到可采性规则把它放进来，而那道开门的裁定就叫 admission。

intro.en: Admit comes from Latin admittere, 'to send in', the same verb that gives admission; English took it through Old French and later reshaped it after the Latin spelling.
intro.cn: admit 来自拉丁语 admittere「送进去」，与 admission 同出一个动词；英语经由古法语借入，后来又按拉丁拼写改写过。

items.en: Mittere meant 'to send, let go', and it also lies behind mission, permit and transmit.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放开」，mission、permit 与 transmit 也都出自它。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus mittere formed admittere, 'to send to, let in, allow to enter'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 mittere 构成 admittere，意为「送到、放进来、准许进入」。

items.en: The past participle admissus meant 'let in, allowed', and it is the form from which the noun admissio was built.
items.cn: 过去分词 admissus 意为「被放进的、获准的」，名词 admissio 正是由这个形式构成。

items.en: Old French amettre meant 'to send, allow'; English borrowed it in the Middle English period and later respelled the word closer to Latin admittere.
items.cn: 古法语 amettre 意为「送出、允许」；英语在中古英语时期借入，后来又把拼写改得更接近拉丁语 admittere。

items.en: The verb is recorded in the fifteenth century for allowing entry; the sense of acknowledging a fact appears in the sixteenth century, and the pattern admit of is established by the seventeenth. Exact dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪有「准许进入」的记录；承认事实的义项见于十六世纪，admit of 这一结构到十七世纪已经确立。确切年代只是近似。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same Latin verb and one word with a different prefix; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of saying that something is true or that entry is allowed.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个拉丁动词的各路形式，以及一个前缀不同的同根词；近义组收其他表示「承认事实」与「允许进入」的说法。

entries.definition: The noun of the same verb, naming the act of letting in or of acknowledging something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，与 admit 同出一源，表示「放行」或「承认」这一行为。

entries.definition: The right to enter, formed with -ance and often seen on official notices.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权」，由 -ance 构成，常见于正式告示。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning 'it must be admitted that'; formed from the past participle plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「诚然、无可否认地」，由过去分词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Allowed to be used as evidence or accepted as valid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的、可接受的」。

entries.definition: To carry out a crime or to promise yourself to something; it shares mittere but not the door of ad-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「犯（罪）、承诺」；与 admit 同出 mittere，但没有 ad- 那扇门的意象。

entries.definition: To admit guilt or wrongdoing, especially in religion or law; heavier in tone than admit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「供认、忏悔」，多用于宗教或法律，语气比 admit 更重。

entries.definition: To accept or recognise that something is true or that someone exists; more formal and often more neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认、认可」，更正式，也常更中性，还可表示「确认收到」。

entries.definition: To admit that something is true only after resisting, usually in an argument or contest.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「让步承认」，往往是在争论或较量中先抵抗再承认。

entries.definition: To let something happen or let someone do something; it names permission, not the acknowledgement of a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「允许」，说的是准许，而不是承认某个事实。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb mittere and the structures admit to and admit of.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 mittere，以及 admit to 与 admit of 这两个结构。

normal.en: Mittere is 'to send', so admit is to send someone in through the door.
normal.cn: mittere 是「送」，所以 admit 就是把某人送进门里。

normal.en: The same verb gives admission, admittance and admissible.
normal.cn: 同一个动词还给出 admission、admittance 与 admissible。

normal.en: Admit to marks the fault you let into the record.
normal.cn: admit to 标出的是你放进记录的那项过错。

normal.en: Be admitted to hospital is the passive of the same doorway.
normal.cn: be admitted to hospital 就是那扇门在被动语态里的样子。

normal.en: Admit of means the situation leaves room for a reading; in the negative it leaves none.
normal.cn: admit of 表示某种情况给某种解读留了余地；用在否定句里就是一点余地都没有。

abstract.en: Picture one doorkeeper doing two jobs at once: letting a visitor in and letting a secret out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个守门人同时做两件事：放一位访客进来，同时放一个秘密出去。

abstract.en: Everything admit does is about crossing a boundary, whether that boundary is a doorway, a rule or a silence.
abstract.cn: admit 做的一切都关乎跨过一道界线，不管这道界线是门框、规矩，还是沉默。

abstract.en: A hall that admits five hundred people and a court that admits a tape are both measuring how much can pass through.
abstract.cn: 能容纳五百人的大厅和采纳一盘录音的法庭，量的都是「允许多少东西通过」。

examples.en: She admitted that she had never read the report.
examples.cn: 她承认自己从未读过那份报告。

examples.en: The club admits new members only after a vote.
examples.cn: 这个俱乐部只有经过投票才会接纳新会员。

examples.en: The hall admits up to five hundred people.
examples.cn: 这个大厅最多可容纳五百人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米特」——阿德把米特从门外拉进来，米特这才低头认了错：准许进入、承认。

root: 拉丁语 admittere「放进来」，过去分词 admissus，由 ad-「向」+ mittere「送」构成；mittere 同时是 mission、permit、transmit 的词根，ad- 带来「朝里」的方向。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses of admit all describe something crossing a boundary: a fact past your silence, a fault past your pride, a person past a door, a student past a rule, a crowd into a hall, a possibility into a reading, or a tape into a courtroom.
sensesIntro.cn: admit 的七个义项都在描述某物跨过一道界线：事实跨过你的沉默、过错跨过你的自尊、一个人跨过门、一名学生跨过规矩、一群人进到厅里、一种可能性进入某种解读，或一盘录音进入法庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorkeeper steps aside and lets someone, or some fact, through the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：守门人侧身让开，放一个人或一个事实通过闸口。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: something kept outside the door of speech is finally let in.
branches.cn: 真相线：一直被挡在言语门外的东西终于被放了进来。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: a person is sent through a real doorway or through the rules of a school.
branches.cn: 机构线：一个人被送过真实的门，或被送过一所学校的规矩。

branches.en: THE SPACE: the building itself becomes the doorkeeper and counts how many it can let through.
branches.cn: 空间线：建筑自己成了守门人，数着自己能放多少人通过。

branches.en: THE POSSIBILITY: a situation lets a reading through, or refuses to.
branches.cn: 可能性线：一种情况放过某种解读，或者拒绝放过。

branches.en: THE COURT: evidence waits outside until the rules of admissibility open the door.
branches.cn: 法庭线：证据在门外等着，直到可采性规则把门打开。

intro.en: Admit is a Latin verb borrowed through French; its endings and the noun admissio supply the rest of the family.
intro.cn: admit 是经法语借入的拉丁动词；它的词尾以及名词 admissio 提供了这一词族的其余成员。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere, admittere, admissus and admissio are all recorded; only the deeper Indo-European root of mittere is reconstructed and its exact form remains uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere、admittere、admissus 与 admissio 均有文献记录；只有 mittere 更早的印欧词根属于重构形式，其确切形态仍不确定。

items.example: It gives the verb its inward direction.
items.exampleCN: 它给动词带来「朝里」的方向。

items.example: It is the root shared by admit and mission.
items.exampleCN: 它是 admit 与 mission 共有的词根。

items.meaning: to send in, let in, allow
items.example: The English verb is a direct borrowing.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词是直接借入的。

items.example: The noun admissio was built on this participle.
items.exampleCN: 名词 admissio 就是在这个分词上构成的。
这个词干出现在 admissible 里。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from ad- and mittere
latinEntries.meaning: to send in, let in, allow to enter
latinEntries.meaningCN: 送进去；放进来；准许进入

definition_zh: 擦；摩擦；揉；擦痕；困难（the rub）
definition_en: to press something against a surface and move it back and forth, or a mark made by rubbing
core_image: 两只手掌来回搓动：压力加上往返移动
scene: 冬天手冷，他不停地搓着双手取暖。 He rubbed his hands together to keep warm in the cold wind.
sceneCN: 这里 rub 是「摩擦」（第 1 个义项：压住并在表面来回移动）；句意：寒风中他搓着双手取暖。

collocations.zh: 往伤口上撒盐；雪上加霜

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 后缀构成，指擦除之物（橡皮）或摩擦产生的材料（橡胶）
一般认为与 rub 同族词形相关，义为「垃圾；废物；胡说」
由 rubbish 加 -y 后缀构成，义为「无价值的；劣质的」

senses.title: To press and move against a surface
senses.definition: to press one thing against a surface and move it backwards and forwards
senses.definitionCN: 把一物压在表面上并来回移动
senses.example: He rubbed his hands together to keep warm.
senses.exampleCN: 他搓着双手取暖。
senses.why: Pressure plus repeated movement is the physical core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 压力加往返移动，是这个词最根本的物理画面。

senses.title: To cause pain or damage by friction
senses.definition: to make skin sore by repeated rubbing
senses.definitionCN: 因反复摩擦使皮肤疼痛或破损
senses.example: The new shoes rubbed my heels badly.
senses.exampleCN: 这双新鞋把我的脚后跟磨得很疼。
senses.why: The same back-and-forth movement harms skin when it repeats too long.
senses.whyCN: 同一种往返动作持续太久，就反过来伤害皮肤。

senses.title: A mark left by rubbing
senses.definition: a dark mark or damage left on a surface by rubbing
senses.definitionCN: 摩擦在表面留下的黑色印记或损伤
senses.example: There is a black rub on the car door.
senses.exampleCN: 车门上有一道黑色的擦痕。
senses.why: The action leaves its trace, so the mark takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 动作会留下痕迹，痕迹便沿用了动作的名字。

senses.title: The difficulty in a situation
senses.definition: the part of a situation that causes problems, used in the phrase the rub is that
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 the rub is that 中指事情里造成麻烦的部分
senses.example: The plan sounds fine; the rub is that we lack money.
senses.exampleCN: 计划听上去不错，问题在于我们没有钱。
senses.why: Friction is what blocks smooth movement, so rubbing names whatever blocks a plan.
senses.whyCN: 摩擦正是阻碍顺滑移动的东西，于是「擦」借指一切卡住计划的障碍。

intro.en: Rub is of uncertain origin; it appeared in Middle English and may be connected with Low German rubben.
intro.cn: rub 词源不确定，见于中古英语，一般认为可能与低地德语 rubben（摩擦）相关。

items.en: Rubben in Low German means to rub, a possible source, though the link is not proven.
items.cn: 低地德语 rubben 意为摩擦，可能是来源之一，但关联尚未确证。

items.en: Rub appears in English in the fourteenth century, already meaning to rub and to scour.
items.cn: 十四世纪 rub 已在英语中出现，兼指摩擦与擦拭。

items.en: Shakespeare popularized the noun sense of difficulty in Hamlet: there's the rub.
items.cn: 莎士比亚在《哈姆雷特》中让名词「症结」义广为流传：there's the rub（难就难在这里）。

items.en: Rubber names the material that rubs out pencil marks, giving both eraser and the elastic substance.
items.cn: rubber 因能擦去铅笔字而得名称「擦除之物」，后兼指弹性材料橡胶。

items.en: Rub extends to idioms about social contact and adding insult to injury.
items.cn: 现代英语中 rub 扩展出社交接触与雪上加霜等习语用法。

note.en: Rub has look-alike family words and near-meaning words about friction and wiping.
note.cn: rub 的形近词多属同族，近义词集中在摩擦与擦拭的义场。

entries.definition: an eraser; the elastic material made from tree sap
entries.definitionCN: 橡皮；橡胶，由 rub 加 -er 构成，因「擦除」功能得名

entries.definition: things thrown away; nonsense
entries.definitionCN: 垃圾；废物；胡说，与 rub 族词形相关，强调被磨掉、被弃之物

entries.definition: one of the curved bones protecting the chest
entries.definitionCN: 肋骨，与 rub 仅一字母之差且常谐音联想，但词源无关，只是形近

entries.definition: to clean something by hard rubbing with a brush
entries.definitionCN: 用力擦洗；刷洗，强调用刷子彻底清洁，比 rub 更用力

entries.definition: to clean a surface by passing a cloth over it
entries.definitionCN: 擦拭；抹，动作轻于 rub，只需一两次划过

entries.definition: to make a surface smooth and shiny by rubbing
entries.definitionCN: 抛光；擦亮，目的在于使表面光亮，rub 只是手段

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember rub through pressure and movement.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕压力与往返移动的记忆路径。

normal.en: RUB your hands on a cold day: rub-a-dub, back and forth.
normal.cn: 冷天搓手：rub-a-dub，来回搓动的节奏就是这个词的声音。

normal.en: A RUBBER rubs out pencil marks: the tool carries the action in its name.
normal.cn: 橡皮（rubber）擦掉铅笔字，工具的名字里就装着这个动作。

normal.en: RUB shoulders with means to bump elbows with people, just like rubbing.
normal.cn: rub shoulders with 是与人擦肩交往，肩与肩相触正像摩擦。

normal.en: There's the RUB: Shakespeare's line for the snag in the plan.
normal.cn: there's the rub 是莎士比亚的名句，指计划中的绊脚石。

normal.en: RUB salt into the wound: rubbing makes everything hurt more.
normal.cn: 往伤口上撒盐（rub salt into the wound）：摩擦只会让痛更痛。

abstract.en: Feel two palms warm each other by moving back and forth.
abstract.cn: 感受两只手掌来回搓动、互相取暖。

abstract.en: See a pencil mark fade away under an eraser's repeated strokes.
abstract.cn: 看铅笔字在橡皮的一次次擦拭中渐渐消失。

abstract.en: Picture a stone blocking the path: the rub that stops the journey.
abstract.cn: 想象挡在路上的一块石头：那就是让行程卡住的「症结」。

examples.en: She rubbed the stain with a wet cloth.
examples.cn: 她用湿布擦拭那块污渍。

examples.en: These new shoes rub my heels terribly.
examples.cn: 这双新鞋把我的脚跟磨得够呛。

examples.en: The plan is good, but the rub is the cost.
examples.cn: 计划不错，但问题就出在成本上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉布」——擦桌子时来回拉扯抹布；rub 读音近似「拉布」

root: 词源不确定，一般认为可能与低地德语 rubben（摩擦）相关，中古英语时期已通用；名词「症结」义由摩擦阻碍移动的意象引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: Rub moves from pressing and moving on a surface, to soreness, to the mark left behind, and finally to whatever blocks a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: rub 从「压住来回移动」出发，引申到磨痛、擦痕，最后借指一切卡住事情的障碍。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pressure plus back-and-forth movement
core.cn: 核心意象：压住表面来回移动

branches.en: Two surfaces pressed together and moved make friction.
branches.cn: 两个表面压在一起来回移动，产生摩擦。

branches.en: The same movement soothes when brief and harms when repeated.
branches.cn: 同一种动作，短暂是安抚，反复太久就磨伤。

branches.en: Rubbing leaves its trace on the surface it works on.
branches.cn: 摩擦在作用过的表面留下自己的痕迹。

branches.en: Friction blocks smooth motion, so rub names the snag in any plan.
branches.cn: 摩擦阻碍顺畅移动，rub 顺势指代计划中的绊脚石。

branches.en: Erasing a mistake and meeting famous people both borrow the rubbing image.
branches.cn: 擦掉错误与和名人擦肩交往，都借用了摩擦的画面。

intro.en: Rub builds a family of erasing, waste, and friction words.
intro.cn: rub 的词族围绕擦除、废物与摩擦展开。

latinIntro.en: Rub is likely Germanic in origin, so it has no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: rub 一般认为属日耳曼语源，没有拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: an eraser; the elastic material from tree sap
items.meaningCN: 橡皮；橡胶（因擦除功能得名，后指弹性材料）
items.exampleCN: 能借用一下你的橡皮吗？

items.example: Take out the rubbish before you leave.
Put the peel in the rubbish bin.

items.meaningCN: 用力擦洗（与 rub 同族的强化形式）
items.example: She scrubbed the floor until it shone.
He rubbed out the wrong answer.
items.exampleCN: 他把写错的答案擦掉了。

items.meaning: to come off by rubbing; to pass on to others
items.meaningCN: 被擦掉；（品质）感染给他人
items.example: His enthusiasm rubbed off on the team.
items.exampleCN: 他的热情感染了整个团队。

items.meaning: to meet and mix with people
items.example: She rubbed shoulders with film stars at the party.
items.exampleCN: 她在聚会上与电影明星们交往。

items.meaningCN: 反复揭人短处；哪壶不开提哪壶
items.example: I lost once; stop rubbing it in.
items.exampleCN: 我就输了一次，别再翻旧账了。

items.meaningCN: 用力擦拭；（运动员的）按摩放松
items.example: The athlete had a rub-down after training.
items.exampleCN: 运动员训练后做了按摩放松。

items.meaning: the hidden difficulty in a situation
items.meaningCN: 症结；难点（固定短语 the rub）
items.example: There's the rub: time is too short.
items.exampleCN: 难就难在这里：时间太短。

definition_zh: 相当大的；相当多的；值得考虑的
definition_en: large enough in amount or degree to be noticed and counted
core_image: 账单上的数字比预想多出一大截
scene: 他打开账单，发现数字比预想多出一大截。 The repair cost a considerable sum.
sceneCN: 这里 considerable 指「相当大的」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度大到值得注意）；句意是这次维修花了一笔相当可观的钱。

pos.zh: 相当大的；相当多的；值得考虑的

derivatives.zh: 相当大地；在很大程度上

senses.title: Large in amount
senses.definition: large enough in amount or degree to be noticed
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度大到值得注意
senses.example: The repair cost a considerable sum.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修花了一笔相当可观的钱。
senses.why: A size that makes you stop and look is a size that counts.
senses.whyCN: 大到让你停下来看的规模，就是有分量的规模。

senses.title: Worth attention
senses.definition: important enough to deserve attention, an older and rarer sense
senses.definitionCN: 重要到值得关注，是较古老且少用的义项
senses.example: It was a considerable event in local history.
senses.exampleCN: 这是地方史上值得重视的事件。
senses.why: What deserves thought is what pulls the eye toward it.
senses.whyCN: 值得思考的东西，会把目光拉向自己。

intro.en: Considerable is consider plus -able, from Latin considerare, to examine, and it first meant able to be considered.
intro.cn: considerable 是 consider 加 -able，源自动词 considerare（审视），最初意为值得被考虑的。

items.en: Considerare meant to examine something closely.
items.cn: considerare 意为仔细审视某物。

items.en: The suffix -abilis marked what could be done.
items.cn: 词尾 -abilis 表示可以被怎样对待。

items.en: French considerable meant worthy of attention.
items.cn: 法语 considerable 意为值得注意的。

items.en: English considerable first meant able to be considered.
items.cn: 英语 considerable 最初指可以被考虑的。

items.en: It shifted to mean great in size or amount.
items.cn: 它的含义转向规模或数量很大。

items.en: Today the size sense is the everyday one.
items.cn: 今天日常使用的主要是表示规模大的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the consider family, and the meaning group names other words for a large amount.
note.cn: 形近组是 consider 家族，近义组列出其他表示数量大的词。

entries.definition: careful about other people's feelings
the act of thinking about something
by a large amount
large in size, value or importance
entries.definitionCN: 规模、价值或重要性大的

entries.definition: great enough to matter
fairly large

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a bill larger than expected, then move to progress you can measure and to an event people still discuss.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从比预想更大的账单开始，再到可以量出的进步，最后到人们仍在谈论的事件。

normal.en: Considerable means big enough that you must consider it.
normal.cn: considerable 就是大到你必须把它考虑进去。

normal.en: A considerable sum is one that changes the plan.
normal.cn: 一笔可观的款子，是能改变计划的那种钱。

normal.en: Considerable progress can be measured, not merely felt.
normal.cn: 相当大的进步是量得出来的，不只是感觉。

normal.en: If nobody would notice its absence, it is not considerable.
normal.cn: 若它不在了也没人察觉，那它就称不上相当大。

normal.en: Think of a shadow long enough to reach the wall.
normal.cn: 想想一道长到能碰到墙的影子。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of coins higher than the cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞比杯子还高的硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a gap in the road you cannot step over.
abstract.cn: 想象路上一道你迈不过去的缺口。

abstract.en: Picture a number that makes a hand pause.
abstract.cn: 想象一个让手停下来的数字。

examples.en: The repair cost a considerable sum.
examples.cn: 这次维修花了一笔相当可观的钱。

examples.en: She spent considerable time on the report.
examples.cn: 她在这份报告上花了相当多的时间。

examples.en: The project made considerable progress this year.
examples.cn: 这个项目今年取得了相当大的进展。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 considerable 记成 consider（考虑）加 able（能）：大到必须被考虑进来的程度，就是相当大的。

root: 由拉丁语 considerare（审视）加 -able 构成，原意是值得被考虑的，后转为数量或程度相当大的。

sensesIntro.en: From something worth thinking about, to a size big enough that it forces itself into your thinking.
sensesIntro.cn: 从值得思考的事物，到大到硬闯进你思考里的规模。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number on a bill that makes the hand pause.
core.cn: 核心意象：账单上一个让手停下来的数字。

branches.en: The main sense is size large enough to be counted.
branches.cn: 主要义项是大到能被计入的规模。

branches.en: The older sense is importance that earns attention.
branches.cn: 较古老的义项是赢得关注的重要性。

branches.en: A large amount of anything becomes important by its weight.
branches.cn: 任何东西的数量一大，就凭分量变得重要。

branches.en: Comparatives like more considerable are rare but regular.
branches.cn: 像 more considerable 这样的比较级少见，但合乎规则。

branches.en: In old texts the word can mean worthy of respect.
branches.cn: 在旧文本里，这个词也可以指值得尊重的。

intro.en: Considerable is consider plus -able, from Latin considerare, to examine.
intro.cn: considerable 是 consider 加 -able，源自动词 considerare（审视）。

latinIntro.cn: 星辰词基 sider- 也出现在 sidereal 以及 desire 的历史中。

items.exampleCN: 体贴的主人会替人续杯。

想休息的愿望占了上风。

definition_zh: 申请；申请书；应用；运用；应用程序；涂抹；敷用；勤奋；专心
definition_en: a formal request, the act of putting something to use, a computer program, or the act of spreading something on a surface
core_image: 一张写满理由的表格被递到窗口，随后又被拿去用起来
scene: 招聘窗口前，年轻人把一叠材料塞进信封。 She sent her application to the university before the deadline.
sceneCN: 这里 application 是「申请；申请书」（第 1 个义项：向机构提出的正式请求）；句意为「她在截止日期前把申请寄给了大学」。画面里有招聘窗口、信封与一叠材料。

pos.zh: 名词：申请；申请书；应用；运用；应用程序；涂抹；勤奋

由 apply 加 -able 构成，义为「适用的；相关的」

senses.title: A formal request
senses.definition: a formal written or spoken request, especially for a job, a place, or permission
senses.definitionCN: 为职位、名额或许可提出的正式书面或口头请求
senses.example: Her application for the scholarship arrived on time.
senses.exampleCN: 她的奖学金申请按时寄到了。
senses.why: Latin applicare meant to attach one thing to another; a request attaches a person to a post or a place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 applicare 意为把一物贴附到另一物上；一份申请就是把一个人附到一个职位或一个地方上。

senses.title: Putting something to use
senses.definition: the act of putting a rule, method, or idea to practical use
senses.definitionCN: 把规则、方法或想法投入实际使用的行为
senses.example: The application of this rule to real cases is not always simple.
senses.exampleCN: 把这条规则应用到真实案例上并不总是简单。
senses.why: The same image of attaching remains: an idea is fastened onto a real situation and made to work there.
senses.whyCN: 「贴附」的意象仍在：一种想法被固定到真实处境上，并在那里起作用。

senses.title: A computer program
senses.definition: a computer program designed for a particular task, especially on a phone or tablet
senses.definitionCN: 为特定任务设计的计算机程序，尤指手机或平板上的程序
senses.example: She installed a language application on her phone.
senses.exampleCN: 她在手机上装了一个语言学习程序。
senses.why: The program is attached to a task the way a tool is applied to work.
senses.whyCN: 程序被贴附到一项任务上，正如工具被用于工作。

senses.title: Spreading a substance
senses.definition: the act of spreading a substance such as cream or paint onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把药膏、涂料一类物质铺到表面上的动作
senses.example: The application of the ointment should be repeated twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药膏应每天涂抹两次。
senses.why: Here applicare is literal: the substance is laid directly onto the skin.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 applicare 是字面义：物质被直接敷到皮肤上。

senses.title: Close attention to work
senses.definition: the quality of working hard and giving close attention to a task
senses.definitionCN: 努力工作并对任务保持专注的品质
senses.example: Success in the course depends on steady application.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课能否学好，取决于能否持续用功。
senses.why: To apply oneself is to attach the whole mind to the work, and the noun keeps that image of close attachment.
senses.whyCN: 投入自己就是把整个心思贴附到工作上，这个名词保留的正是那种紧密贴附的意象。

intro.en: Application is built on the Latin verb applicare, and its whole history is the history of attaching one thing to another.
intro.cn: application 建立在拉丁语动词 applicare 之上，它的整段历史就是「把一物贴到另一物」的历史。

items.en: 「*plek-」 is reconstructed with the sense 'to weave, plait, fold'. The deeper origin of this root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语「*plek-」被重构为「编织、折叠」的意思；这个更早的来源存疑。

items.en: Plicare meant 'to fold', and its compounds carry the idea of laying one thing onto another.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」，它的复合词带有把一物铺到另一物上的意思。

items.en: Ad- plus plicare gave applicare, 'to attach, put to, apply'; the noun applicatio follows the same pattern.
items.cn: ad- 与 plicare 构成 applicare，意为「贴附、施加、应用」；名词 applicatio 沿同一路径而来。

items.en: Old French aplier and its derived noun enter English usage after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 aplier 及其派生名词在诺曼时期之后进入英语用法。

items.en: The word splits into a request, a use, a coating, a program and a habit of diligence.
items.cn: 这个词分成申请、运用、涂抹、程序与勤奋几种用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family built on apply; the near-meaning group gathers words for requests, use and diligence.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 apply 之上的一族词；近义组收表示请求、使用与勤奋的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to request, use, or spread.
entries.definitionCN: 本词由它加后缀构成，义为「申请、使用、涂抹」的动词。

entries.definition: A person who makes a formal request.
entries.definitionCN: 提出正式申请的人，即「申请人」。

entries.definition: Able to be applied or relevant to a particular case.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「适用的、相关的」。

entries.definition: A device for spreading a substance on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「涂抹器、敷料器」。

entries.definition: An act of asking for something in a polite or formal way.
entries.definitionCN: 以礼貌或正式方式提出请求的行为，对应 application 的申请义。

entries.definition: A formal written appeal, often signed by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 常由多人签名的正式书面请愿，与申请书相近。

entries.definition: The way in which something is used, or the amount of use.
entries.definitionCN: 某物被使用的方式或使用量，对应 application 的应用义。

entries.definition: Careful and persistent effort in work.
entries.definitionCN: 工作中细心而持续的努力，对应 application 的勤奋义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the Latin image of attaching one thing to another.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子沿着拉丁语「把一物贴到另一物」的意象展开。

normal.en: A request attaches you to a post: a job application.
normal.cn: 申请把你附到一个职位上：求职申请。

normal.en: An idea attached to reality is its application.
normal.cn: 想法贴到现实上，就是它的应用。

normal.en: A program is a tool attached to a task.
normal.cn: 程序是被贴到任务上的工具。

normal.en: Applying yourself means attaching the whole mind.
normal.cn: 投入自己就是把整个心思贴上去。

abstract.cn: 一个表示贴附的动词，生出表格、用途、程序与美德。

abstract.cn: 这个词总在连接两样东西：人与职位、规则与案例。

abstract.en: Its range shows how paperwork and technology share one image.
abstract.cn: 它的范围显示文书与技术共享同一个意象。

examples.cn: 她在截止日期前把申请寄给了大学。

examples.en: The application of this rule to real cases is not always simple.
examples.cn: 把这条规则应用到真实案例上并不总是简单。

examples.en: He praised her steady application to the research.
examples.cn: 他称赞她对研究持续用功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普里凯申」——把一张申请表贴在职位门口：申请；应用

root: application 来自拉丁语 applicare「贴附、施加」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 plicare「折叠」构成，更早的印欧词根形式存疑。经古法语进入英语后，这个词一方面指把请求递交上去的申请与申请书，另一方面指把规则、想法、药膏贴到对象上的应用与涂抹；现代又添了计算机应用程序与勤奋、专心两层用法。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses all keep the Latin image of attaching: a request, a rule put to work, a program, a cream spread on skin, and a mind fixed on study.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法都保留拉丁语「贴附」的意象：一份请求、一条被拿去用的规则、一个程序、一层涂在皮肤上的药膏，以及一颗钉在学业上的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a filled form pressed onto a desk, then a tool pressed onto a task.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张填好的表格被按到桌上，随后工具被按到任务上。

branches.en: THE REQUEST LINE: a person is attached to a post or a place.

branches.cn: 运用线：一种想法被贴附到真实处境上。

branches.en: THE PROGRAM LINE: a tool is attached to a task.
branches.cn: 程序线：工具被贴附到一项任务上。

branches.en: THE COATING LINE: a substance is laid onto a surface.
branches.cn: 涂抹线：物质被铺到表面上。

branches.en: THE DILIGENCE LINE: the whole mind is attached to the work.
branches.cn: 勤奋线：整个心思被贴附到工作上。

intro.en: Application is a transparent derivative of apply: the verb plus the noun suffix -ation.

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is real: applicare 'attach' and plicare 'fold' are the ancestors of the word.

definition_en: the line that divides two countries
core_image: 山口上立着的界碑
scene: 两国的界碑立在山口。 They crossed the border at a small mountain pass.
sceneCN: 这里 border 是「边界；国界」（第 1 个义项：两国之间的分界线）；句意是他们在一个小山口越过边界。

senses.title: A line between countries
senses.definition: the line that separates two countries
senses.definitionCN: 分隔两个国家的界线
senses.example: They crossed the border at a small mountain pass.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一个小山口越过边界。
senses.why: This is the strongest modern sense, from a word for an edge.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常用的义项，来自表示边缘的词。

senses.title: The outer edge
senses.definition: the outer part of a surface or an object
senses.definitionCN: 表面或物体的外沿部分
senses.example: The rug has a red border.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地毯有一圈红色的边。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply an edge, and a country line is one kind of edge.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是边缘，国界只是其中一种边缘。

senses.title: To be next to
senses.definition: to have a border next to a place
senses.definitionCN: 与某地相邻、共用边界
senses.example: France borders Germany to the east.
senses.exampleCN: 法国东边与德国接壤。
senses.why: The noun became a verb meaning to share an edge.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，表示共用一条边。

definition_zh: 药丸；药片；避孕药；讨厌的人（非正式）
definition_en: a small solid round piece of medicine that you swallow whole
core_image: 一颗能整个吞下的小圆球，苦味藏在糖衣里
scene: 护士倒了一杯温水递过去，示意她仰头把那颗小圆球咽下去。 She swallowed the pill with a sip of water.
sceneCN: 这里是「药丸」（第 1 个义项：小粒固体内服药）；句意为她就着一口水把药丸咽下。画面里就是那颗顺着喉咙滑下去的小圆球。

pos.zh: 药丸；药片；口服避孕药；讨厌鬼

derivatives.zh: pill 与 box 的复合词，义为「药丸盒；盒式帽」
旧式复合词，义为「制药者；药剂师」
罕用派生词，义为「用药丸的人」

senses.title: A small round dose of medicine
senses.definition: a small solid piece of medicine made to be swallowed whole
senses.definitionCN: 制成小粒、可整颗吞服的固体药物
senses.example: The doctor prescribed one pill each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 医生开了药，每天早晨一粒。
senses.why: Latin pilula is a little ball, and the medicine takes the shape of its name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pilula 意为小球，药采用了它名字所指的形状。

senses.title: Oral contraception
senses.definition: the pill, a daily medicine that prevents pregnancy
senses.definitionCN: 指「the pill」，每日服用以避孕的药
senses.example: She started taking the pill in her twenties.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十多岁开始服用避孕药。
senses.why: One medicine became so common that its common noun with the article names it alone.
senses.whyCN: 一种药太常用，以致带定冠词的普通名词单独指它。

senses.title: Something unpleasant that must be accepted
senses.titleCN: 难以接受的事（a bitter pill）
senses.definition: a fact or loss that is hard to accept
senses.definitionCN: 难以接受的事实或损失
senses.example: Losing to a rival team was a bitter pill to swallow.
senses.exampleCN: 输给宿敌令人难以接受。
senses.why: The taste of medicine transfers to the taste of bad news.
senses.whyCN: 药的苦味转移到了坏消息的味道上。

senses.title: An annoying person
senses.definition: an annoying or tiresome person, American informal
senses.definitionCN: 令人恼火或厌烦的人，美式非正式
senses.example: Her little brother can be a real pill on long drives.
senses.exampleCN: 她弟弟长途坐车时实在烦人。
senses.why: The person becomes the medicine you are forced to swallow again and again.
senses.whyCN: 这个人变成了你不得不一次次吞下的那剂药。

senses.title: To form into pills
senses.definition: to roll medicine or food into small round pieces
senses.definitionCN: 把药物或食物搓成小圆粒
senses.example: The pharmacist pilled the herb paste by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 药剂师手工把药膏搓成丸。
senses.why: The noun names the result, and the verb names the making of it.
senses.whyCN: 名词指成品，动词指把它做出来的过程。

senses.title: A pellet or ball of anything
senses.definition: a small ball of any substance, such as lint or dough
senses.definitionCN: 任何物质的小球粒，如毛球或面团球
senses.example: Sweaters collect little pills after many washes.
senses.exampleCN: 毛衣多次洗涤后会起小球。
senses.why: The shape, not the substance, carries the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 承载意义的是形状，而非材料。

senses.title: Pill-popping, habitual medication
senses.definition: frequent casual use of pills, often without medical need
senses.definitionCN: 频繁随意服药，往往并无医疗必要
senses.example: The film shows a pill-popping society unable to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 影片描绘了一个靠药丸度日、无法入睡的社会。
senses.why: When doses multiply, the pill stops being a cure and becomes a habit.
senses.whyCN: 当服用次数倍增，药丸不再是治疗，而成习惯。

intro.en: Pill comes from Latin pilula, a little ball, a diminutive of pila, the same ball-shaped stone that gave pile; the path ran through Middle Dutch and Middle English.
intro.cn: pill 来自拉丁语 pilula（小球），是 pila 的指小形式，与 pile 同源；路径经由中古荷兰语与中古英语。

items.en: Pila meant a ball or pillar; pilula, its diminutive, meant a little ball.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pila 指球或柱；其指小形式 pilula 意为小球。

items.en: Middle Dutch pile and Middle Low German pille carried the medicine sense northward.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 pile 与中古低地德语 pille 把药丸义带向北方。

items.en: Pill appeared in fourteenth-century English for a rolled medicine.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语已用 pill 指搓制的药丸。

items.en: The idiom a bitter pill and the verb to pill grew inside English.
items.cn: a bitter pill 的习语和动词 to pill 都在英语内部生长。

items.en: The twentieth century added the pill for contraception and pillbox hats and cases.
items.cn: 二十世纪又添了 the pill（避孕药）以及 pillbox 帽和药盒。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the ball-shaped family and two deceiving neighbours; the near-meaning group gathers dosage words.
note.cn: 形近组收球形词族和两个易混词；近义组收剂型用语。

entries.definitionCN: 小药丸，几乎原样保留拉丁指小形式。

entries.definitionCN: 装有药物的可溶胶囊，源自拉丁语「小盒」。

normalIntro.en: One picture does the work: a small ball travelling down the throat.
normalIntro.cn: 一幅画面足矣：一颗小球顺喉而下。

normal.en: Latin pilula is literally little ball — the pill is a ball you swallow.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pilula 字面即小球——药丸就是你吞下的球。

normal.en: Pill and pile share the Latin pila; one shrank to a ball, the other grew into a heap.
normal.cn: pill 与 pile 共享拉丁 pila；一个缩成小球，一个堆成大堆。

normal.en: The pill without a number still means one specific medicine in modern speech.
normal.cn: 现代口语中，不带数字的 the pill 特指一种药。

normal.en: A bitter pill to swallow matches taste to truth: bad facts taste like medicine.
normal.cn: a bitter pill to swallow 把味道对上事实：坏消息尝起来像药。

normal.en: Pills on a sweater are also little balls — the shape meaning never left.
normal.cn: 毛衣上的毛球也是小球——形状义从未离开。

abstract.en: The smallest container of relief: an entire cure in one round shell.
abstract.cn: 最小的缓解容器：整个疗法装进一个圆壳。

abstract.en: Swallowing is agreeing: the idiom makes acceptance an act of the throat.
abstract.cn: 吞咽即接受：习语把「接受」变成喉咙的动作。

abstract.en: From the pharmacist's hand to the sweater's cuff, the little ball keeps rolling through the language.
abstract.cn: 从药剂师的手到毛衣的袖口，小球在语言里一路滚下去。

examples.en: Take one pill after every meal.
examples.cn: 每餐后服一粒药。

examples.en: The defeat was a bitter pill for the whole team.
examples.cn: 这场失败让全队难以接受。

examples.en: My old sweater is covered in little pills.
examples.cn: 我的旧毛衣起了一层小球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮欧」——皮蛋大小的药丸一口吞下，皮欧一声就进肚；pill 就是药丸。

root: 拉丁语 pila（球、柱）的指小形式 pilula（小球）经中古荷兰语进入中古英语成为 pill；核心意象始终是小圆球。

sensesIntro.en: The little ball of Latin grows through medicine into money slang, moral idiom, a nuisance person and even the fuzz on a sweater.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁的小球经由医药长出金钱俚语、道德习语、讨厌鬼，甚至毛衣上的毛球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smooth little ball that goes down whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗整个咽下的光滑小球。

branches.en: a round dose in the palm of a hand
branches.cn: 掌心里的一粒圆药

branches.en: a packet opened every morning
branches.cn: 每天早晨拆开的一板药

branches.en: a face forcing down hard news
branches.cn: 强咽坏消息的脸

branches.en: a back-seat brother asking questions nonstop
branches.cn: 后座上问个不停的弟弟

branches.en: the same ball of lint and of medicine
branches.cn: 同是小球：毛球与药丸

intro.en: The word family is small: the Latin diminutive plus a few English compounds.
intro.cn: 词族很小：拉丁指小形式加若干英语复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pilula stands behind the whole group; no other Latin terms are needed.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族背后是拉丁语 pilula；无需其他拉丁词。

definition_en: a small round piece of medicine, a flat slab with writing on it, or a thin portable computer
core_image: 掌心大小的扁平薄片
scene: 医生把一片白色药片放在桌上，叮嘱她饭后服用。 The doctor put a white tablet on the table and told her to take it after meals.
sceneCN: 这里 tablet 是「药片」（第 1 个义项）；句意：医生把一片白色药片放在桌上，叮嘱她饭后服用。

senses.title: A small round pill
senses.definition: a small round piece of medicine that you swallow
senses.definitionCN: 吞服的小圆片药物
senses.example: The doctor put a white tablet on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把一片白色药片放在桌上。
senses.why: A flat pressed disc of medicine keeps the shape of a small board.
senses.whyCN: 压制成型的小药片保留了「扁平一片」的形状，所以从木板转指药片。

senses.title: A flat slab with writing
senses.definition: a flat piece of stone or metal with words cut into it
senses.definitionCN: 刻有文字的扁平石板或金属板
senses.example: The names were cut into a stone tablet.
senses.exampleCN: 名字被刻在石碑上。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a flat board used for writing.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是用来书写的平板，石碑与牌匾都沿用了这块「平板」的形象。

senses.title: A thin portable computer
senses.definition: a thin flat computer that you control by touching the screen
senses.definitionCN: 靠触摸屏幕操作的薄型电脑
senses.example: She reads the news on her tablet every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上用平板电脑看新闻。
senses.why: The device is literally a flat slate you write and read on.
senses.whyCN: 这种设备本质上就是一块可读可写的扁平石板，于是沿用 tablet 这个名字。

intro.en: Tablet descends from Latin tabula, a board, through a small-board form.
intro.cn: tablet 经由「小板」这一指小形式，源自拉丁语 tabula（木板、书写板）。

items.en: Tabula meant a board or writing tablet.
items.cn: tabula 意为木板或书写板。

items.en: Tabella was the small form of tabula.
items.cn: tabella 是 tabula 的指小形式，意为小板。

items.en: Tablete named a small board.
items.cn: tablete 指小块板子。

items.en: Tablette kept the board sense.
items.cn: tablette 保留了「板」的含义。

items.en: Tablet extended to pills and flat computers.
items.cn: tablet 后来扩展到药片与平板电脑。

note.en: Tablet is set beside look-alike words and beside words for pills and flat devices.
note.cn: 把 tablet 与形近词，以及表示药片和扁平设备的词作对比。

entries.definition: a piece of furniture with a flat top
a small flap or label
arranged in rows and columns
a small round medicine
a medicine inside a shell
a flat piece of stone

normalIntro.en: A tablet is a flat piece you can hold, whether it holds words, medicine, or a screen.
normalIntro.cn: tablet 是手中一块扁平的东西，上面可以写字、装药或显示屏幕。

normal.en: The doctor put a white tablet on the table.
normal.cn: 医生把一片白色药片放在桌上。

normal.en: She reads the news on her tablet every morning.
normal.cn: 她每天早上用平板电脑看新闻。

normal.en: The names were cut into a stone tablet.
normal.cn: 名字被刻在石碑上。

normal.en: Take one tablet after each meal.
normal.cn: 每餐后服用一片药。

normal.en: The tablet screen is easy to carry.
normal.cn: 平板电脑的屏幕轻薄易携带。

abstract.en: One flat shape serves stone, medicine, and glass.
abstract.cn: 同一个扁平形状，服务石头、药物与玻璃。

abstract.en: A board that learned to heal and to glow.
abstract.cn: 一块板学会了治病，也学会了发光。

abstract.en: Flatness is the thread through all three meanings.
abstract.cn: 「扁平」是贯穿三个义项的线索。

examples.en: The doctor put a white tablet on the table.
examples.cn: 医生把一片白色药片放在桌上。

examples.en: She reads the news on her tablet every morning.
examples.cn: 她每天早上用平板电脑看新闻。
